data.title: This video features an interview with Noam Chomsky
data.content:
## Summary
This video features an interview with Noam Chomsky and a technical critique of Yann LeCun’s paper on autonomous machine intelligence. The host explores the divide between connectionist approaches to AI and the necessity of symbolic compositionality for true reasoning.

## Key Points
- Yann LeCun's paper 'A Path Towards Autonomous Machine Intelligence' proposes world models as internal predictive systems for AI.
- The host argues that current LLMs and neural networks lack 'intentionality' and the ability to represent infinite objects via symbolic logic.
- A conflict is highlighted between the empiricist 'blank slate' view (LeCun, Sutton) and the rationalist view (Chomsky).
- Jürgen Schmidhuber claims LeCun's 2022 paper fails to cite his lab's foundational work on controllers and world models from the 1990s.
- Compositionality and systematicity are presented as essential requirements for AI to achieve human-level planning and semantics.

## AI Concepts
World Models, Autonomous Machine Intelligence, Energy-Based Models (EBM), Joint Embedding Prediction Architecture (JEPA), Self-supervised Learning, Compositional Semantics, Systematicity, Inductive Bias, Latent Variables, System 2 Reasoning
